explanation: Compare the target with the current BST key and follow the only subtree that can contain it. Return -1 after reaching a missing child.
timeComplexity: O(h) for tree height h. Only one search branch is taken per level; recursive variants also retain their call frames.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Iteration uses only a cursor; recursion retains one frame per tree level.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: If the current key is not the target, the BST ordering places any matching key exclusively in the chosen left or right subtree. Each step preserves the possibility of finding the target while discarding only impossible keys. A missing child proves absence; an equality returns the requested key.
walkthrough: For tree [11,5,16,2,8,13,19] and key 13, 13>11 sends the search right to 16; 13<16 sends it left to 13. Equality returns 13. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: A target equal to the root is returned immediately.
A missing target ends at a null child.
The return is the key value, not a node index.
